title: Gorkut Ata
kicker: Literature · the Oghuz epic, 14th–15th centuries to today

blocks.tk: Oguzlaryň rowaýatlarynda Gorkut Ata paýhasly ýaşuly, bagşy we geljegi aýdýan adam. Rowaýata görä, ol 295 ýyl ýaşapdyr. Onuň adyny göterýän kitap, “Kitaby Dädem Gorkut”, oguzlaryň iň meşhur dessany. Kitapda bir giriş we on iki hekaýa bar. Olar esasan kyssa, ýöne içinde goşgular hem köp.
blocks.en: In the legends of the Oghuz, Gorkut Ata, Dede Korkut or Grandfather Korkut, is a wise elder, a bard and a seer. The 14th-century historian Rashid al-Din describes him as a real man who lived for 295 years: a legend, not a record. The book that bears his name, the Book of Dede Korkut (Kitaby Dädem Gorkut in Turkmen), is the best-known epic of the Oghuz, the Turkic tribes whose heritage the Turkmen share with the peoples of Azerbaijan and Türkiye. It has a prologue and twelve stories, told mostly in prose; the verse, some two thousand lines, makes up about a third of the text.

blocks.tk: Hekaýalarda oguz begleri we olaryň aýallary söweşýärler, aw awlaýarlar, toý tutýarlar we ýesirleri boşadýarlar. Iň meşhur hekaýalaryň birinde Basat ýigit adam iýýän Ýekegözi ýeňýär. Bu hekaýa Gomeriň Siklop hakyndaky hekaýasyna meňzeýär. Salyr Gazan, Bamsy Beýrek ýaly gahrymanlar hem bar. Gorkut Ata ýaş ýigitlere at dakyp beripdir. Kyn meselelerde oguzlar oňa ýüz tutupdyrlar. Her hekaýanyň ahyrynda ol gelip, saz çalyp, bolan wakany aýdyp beripdir we diňleýänlere ýagşy dilegler edipdir.
blocks.en: The stories follow the lords and ladies of the Oghuz as they fight, hunt, feast and free captives. In one of the most famous, the young Basat kills Tepegöz, a one-eyed giant who eats people, a tale often compared with Odysseus and the Cyclops. Other heroes include Salur Kazan and Bamsi Beyrek. Dede Korkut gives boys their names as they come of age, such as Bugach and Beyrek; the Oghuz turn to him in hard matters; and at the feast that closes each tale he arrives with his kopuz, a lute, sings the story as his own and blesses the listeners.

blocks.tk: Alymlaryň pikirine görä, bu hekaýalary asyrlaryň dowamynda ozanlar dilden aýdypdyrlar, soňra 14-nji ýa-da 15-nji asyrda kimdir biri olary kitap edip ýazypdyr. Kitabyň iki golýazmasy köpden bäri belli: biri Drezdende, beýlekisi Watikanda. Drezden golýazmasynda on iki hekaýanyň hemmesi bar. 2018-nji ýylda alymlar Eýranyň demirgazygynda, türkmenleriň köp ýaşaýan ýerinde, üçünji golýazmany tapdylar.
blocks.en: Scholars think the stories were sung for centuries by bards called ozan before an unknown scribe wrote them down, probably in the 14th or 15th century; the exact date is debated. For a long time two manuscripts were known: one in Dresden, with all twelve stories, and one in the Vatican Library, found by Ettore Rossi in 1950. In 2018 a third turned up in a private collection in Gonbad-e Kavus, in northern Iran, a city of the Turkmen Sahra region; scholars call it the Turkmen Sahra manuscript.

blocks.tk: Türkmenistanda bu dessanyň ady “Gorkut Ata”. 1940-njy we 1950-nji ýyllarda folklorçy Ata Rahmanow Daşoguz welaýatynda garry bagşylardan Gorkut Ata hakynda hekaýalary ýazyp alypdyr. Olaryň biri şol wagt segsen dokuz ýaşyndady. Bu türkmen wariantlarynyň birinde on alty hekaýa bar. Olaryň dördüsi Drezden golýazmasynda ýok: meselem, Gorkut Atanyň mazary barada hekaýa.
blocks.en: In Turkmenistan the epic goes by its hero's name, Gorkut Ata. In the 1940s and 1950s the folklorist Ata Rahmanov wrote down Gorkut Ata tales from elderly storytellers around Boldumsaz, in Dashoguz province, one of them 89 years old. According to Melek Erdem's study of these Turkmen variants (1998), one of them has sixteen stories, four of which, among them Igdir and a tale about the digging of Gorkut's grave, are not in the Dresden manuscript.

blocks.tk: Türkmen alymy Meti Köseýew 1945–1946-njy ýyllarda on iki hekaýany türkmen dilinde çap edipdir. Ýöne onuň taýýarlan kitaby şol wagt çykmandyr: ol diňe 1990-njy ýylda çykdy. Garaşsyzlykdan soň kitabyň täze neşirleri hem çykdy. Häzir türkmen alymlary Gorkut Atany türkmenleriň milli dessanlarynyň biri hasaplaýarlar. Olaryň pikirine görä, hekaýalardaky ýerleriň köpüsi Syrderýanyň, Aral deňziniň we Balkan daglarynyň töwereginde.
blocks.en: Meti Köseýew published the twelve Dresden stories in Turkmen in the journal Sowet edebiýaty in 1945–1946. A book he prepared for 1951 was banned and he was imprisoned until 1956; his Gorkut Ata came out only in 1990, and further editions have followed, according to Halil İbrahim Şahin's survey of Dede Korkut research in Turkmenistan. Turkmen scholars count Gorkut Ata among the national epics of the Turkmen and, Şahin reports, place much of its geography along the Syr Darya, the Aral Sea and the Balkan mountains.

blocks.tk: 2018-nji ýylda Gorkut Ata bilen baglanyşykly epik medeniýet, ertekiler we saz UNESKO-nyň sanawyna girdi. Bu sanawda on iki rowaýat we on üç saz eseri bar. Bu sanaw üçin hödürnamany Azerbaýjan, Gazagystan we Türkiýe bilelikde berdiler.
blocks.en: In 2018 the epic culture, folk tales and music of Dede Korkut, twelve legends and thirteen traditional melodies, joined UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, in a joint file from Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Türkiye.

blocks.title: Reading the Turkmen
blocks.text: Look for this unit's helpers: *at dakyp beripdir* (he gave them names, **for them**), *aýdyp beripdir* (he told it **to them**), *ýazyp alypdyr* (he wrote them down, **to keep**). And a reason in one clause: *çözüp bilmändikleri üçin*, because they couldn't solve it.

vocab.en: epic, a long tale in verse and prose

questions.q: How many stories does the Dresden manuscript contain?
